input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 grants HDI (counterparty) an inspection right against us. It already satisfies three playbook elements — 30 days' prior written notice, normal business hours, and HDI bearing inspection costs — but it places no cap on frequency (unlimited inspections), imposes no confidentiality/independent-auditor requirement, and does not exclude access to our systems. The redline adds a once-per-12-months cap, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, off-site conduct where practicable, and a bar on direct or remote system access, reaching the preferred position with minimal edits. We deliberately did not add the >5% underpayment cost-shift, since the current unconditional HDI cost allocation is more favorable to us.

proposal.summary: Cap inspection frequency at once per 12 months, require an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and bar access to Company systems.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We limited HDI's inspection right to once in any twelve-month period, required it to be conducted by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality and off-site where practicable, and excluded any access to our systems or networks; the existing 30 days' notice, business-hours and HDI-cost terms already meet our position. If helpful, we can accept an annual on-site review of the relevant records only, still at HDI's cost.
